sentences.text:
Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K. Lakshman
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 Writ Petition No.27606 Of 2024
Oral Order

:
Heard Mr. Yadu Krishna Sainath, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 4 and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing on behalf of respondent No.5.
Perused the record.
2. In view of the nature of relief sought for in this Writ Petition, notice to unofficial respondent Nos.6 to 9 is dispensed with.

3. This Writ Petition is filed seeking to declare the action of the respondents, more particularly respondent No.4 in binding over the petitioner under Sections - 126, 127, 128 and 129 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') on the request made by respondent No.5 and obtaining bond on 30.08.2024 vide Form No.13 for a period of six months without following due process of law as illegal and arbitrary, and

for consequential direction to the respondents to permit him to do KL,J cultivation/agricultural operations on his land in Survey No.74/1/A, admeasuring Acs.14.09 guntas, situated at Gurvapur Village, Kasipet Mandal,
Mancherial District.

4. The petitioner is claiming that he is the absolute owner and possessor of land admeasuring Ac.14.0900 gts., in Sy.No.74/1/A, situated at Gurvapur Village, Kasipet Mandal, Mancherial District,
on the strength of a registered sale deed vide Document No.334 of 2020, dated 11.02.2020.

According to him, respondent Nos.6 to 9 are continuously interfering with his possession under the guise of forged sale deeds and also threatened him to sell the subject land to them under the mediation of respondent No.4.
He gave a report with respondent No.5 against the respondent Nos.6 to 9.
However, the police, instead of registering FIR, advised him to settle the matter, otherwise, his life would be in danger, as respondent Nos.6 to 9 are having political influence.

Further, the petitioner enquired about the ownership and title of adjacent land i.e., Sy.No.74/1 with respondent No.4 and obtained copies of sale deeds which the unofficial respondents have created by impersonating a dead person.

The petitioner has KL,J filed sale deeds of respondent Nos.6 to 9 vide registered Document Nos.13287 of 2016, dated 26.10.2016, 13288 of 2016, 13293 of 2016, and 13294 of 2016, dated 25.10.2016 and further submitted that in all the above sale deeds, one Yousuf Ali Baig is the vendor who died on 15.04.2011, i.e., much prior to execution of sale deeds in favour of unofficial respondents.

He further submitted that the Judgment dated 22.11.2022 passed by learned XX Junior Civil Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad in O.S.No.1549 of 2021 would also reflect that Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/
1 Yousuf Ali Baig, who is the vendor of unofficial respondent Nos.6 to 9 died on 15.04.2011, which is clearly an impersonation of dead person at the time of registration of the sale deeds.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further stated that he has also submitted several representations to respondent Nos.1 to 5 along with documentary evidence.
However, no action has been taken against respondent Nos.6 to 9 as they are influential persons.

5. While matter stood thus, pursuant to the report submitted by respondent No.5 on 30.08.2024,
respondent No.4 bound over the petitioner under Sections - 126, 127, 128 and 129 of the BNSS by way of accepting bonds for keeping good behavior for a period KL,J of six (06) months forcibly, or else to forfeit an amount of Rs.50,000/- without following any procedure laid down under law.

On account of the said action of respondent Nos.4 and 5, the petitioner herein is unable to attend agricultural operations on the subject land by way of cultivation, and thereby his livelihood is being affected.

6. Perusal of record would show that respondent Nos.6 to 9 said to have created sale deeds and got registered the adjacent property in their names as their Vendor died much prior to the execution of the said sale deeds i.e., 15.04.2011.
However, it is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the police have no power to make a requisition under Section - 129 of the BNSS.
There is a procedure prescribed to pass an order under Section - 129 (e) of the BNSS.
The police have not followed the said procedure in the present case.

Even, respondent No.4 did not follow the procedure laid down under Section - 129 of the BNSS which corresponds to Section - 110 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, while binding over the petitioner herein.
KL,J 7.

In view of the above submission, it is apt to refer to Section - 129 of the BNSS, which is as under:
"129. Security for good behaviour from habitual offenders.

When an Executive Magistrate receives information that there is within his local jurisdiction a person who- (a) - - - - -,
(b) - - - - -, or (c) - - - - -, or (d) - - - - -, or (e) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of, offences,
involving a breach of the peace, or (f) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of-

Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/
2

entities.text: Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) any offence under one or more of the following.
Thus, procedure is prescribed under Section - 129 of the BNSS to be followed before binding over the petitioner.
But, the police without following the said procedure have made requisition under Section - 129 of the BNSS.

8. It is apt to note that Section - 129 of the BNSS deals with 'security for good behaviour from habitual offenders', and the Executive Magistrate has to make an order under Section - 130 of the BNSS setting forth the substance of the information received, the amount of bond to be executed,
the term for which it is to be in force and the number, character and class of sureties (if any)
required.
9. It is also relevant to note that Chapter - XIII of the BNSS deals with 'information to the police and their powers to investigate'.

As per Section - 173 (1) of the BNSS, every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge KL,J of a police station, and if given (i) orally, it shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant; and every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing as aforesaid,
shall be signed by the person giving it; (ii) by electronic communication, it shall be taken on record by him on being signed within three days by the person giving it, and the substance thereof shall be entered in a book to be kept by such Officer in such form as the State Government may by rules Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/
3 prescribe in this behalf.
10.

sentences.text:
Whereas, in the present case, respondent No.5 while making requisition by producing the petitioner before respondent No.4 did not mention the details/particulars of crimes registered against the petitioner except stating that the petitioner is obstructing cultivation of Survey No.74/1,
admeasuring Acs.9.17, Survey Nos.74/1/AA, 74/1/1E and 74/1/1, situated at Guruvapur Village and,
therefore, the petitioner is produced before respondent No.4.
Further, respondent No.4 did not follow the procedure laid down under Section - 130 of the BNSS before binding over the petitioner.

In fact, Section - 129 (e) of the BNSS is not a penal KL,J provision under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and is only a procedure under the BNSS for the purpose of securing good behaviour from the habitual offender.
11. As already stated above, Section - 110 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is corresponding to Section- 129 of the BNSS.

In Banala Subhashini v. The State of Telangana 1, this Court had an occasion to deal with the scope and ambit of Section - 145 of the Code the powers of the Executive Magistrate, and by relying upon various judgments of Apex Court, it had held that the Executive Magistrate cannot pass any order, once there is anything to say that prima facie, any person in possession and once there is a civil matter pending.

entities.text: Banala Subhashini v. The State of Telangana 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In view of the said procedure and the principle laid down in the aforesaid decision, coming to the present case, as discussed above, there are no civil cases pending against the subject property.
Despite receipt of report from the petitioner, respondent No.4 did not take any action.

On the other hand, it is the specific contention of the petitioner that the unofficial . 2017 SCC Online Hyd. 140 KL,J respondents with an intention to grab the subject property are interfering with the possession of the petitioner.

Without considering all the said aspects, the act of respondent No.5 making requisition to respondent No.4, who in turn, without following the procedure laid down under law as mentioned above, obtained bond in Form No.13 binding over the petitioner for Rs.50,000/- to maintain good behaviour for a period of six (06) months or else to forfeit the said amount is illegal.
13. As stated above, there is a procedure prescribed under Section - 129 of the BNSS to be followed.

As per the said Section, when an Executive Magistrate receives information within his local jurisdiction, a person who, habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of offences, involving a breach of the peace, such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided,
require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond, with sureties,
for his good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three (03) years, as the Magistrate thinks fit.
He has to make an order under Section - 130 of the BNSS.

Without following the said procedure,
respondent No.4 KL,J bound over the petitioner.
Thus, respondent No.4 has not followed the procedure laid down under Section - 129 of the BNSS, more particularly Section - 129 (e).

As stated above, if at all respondent No.5 is having any such law and order problem, he has to submit information to respondent No.4 with all supporting documents in accordance with Section - 129 of the BNSS with a request to bind over the habitual offenders in order to secure good behaviour.
Respondent No.4 has to follow the procedure laid down under Section - 129 of the Code by issuing show-cause notice and he shall pass an order under Section - 130 of the BNSS.
But, respondent No.4 did not follow the said procedure.

In fact, in the impugned order dated 30.08.2024, respondent Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/
4 No.4 did not mention the details of criminal cases pending against the petitioner.

sentences.text: Therefore, viewed from any angle, the order of binding over the petitioner dated 30.08.2024 by respondent No.4 in Form No.13 is illegal and liable to be quashed.

14. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed, and the order of binding over the petitioner, dated 30.08.2024 passed by respondent No.4 for a period of six (06) months vide Form No.13 KL,J in Case Register No.73 of 2024 pursuant to the requisition made by respondent No.5 under Sections - 126, 127, 128 and 129 of the BNSS is hereby set aside declaring the same as illegal.
In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.

_________________ K. LAKSHMAN, J 03.10.2024 Pvt Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/
